content.comment_body: Hello, I am a student starting with [company_name] [product_name] and I want to control the analog output so it provides 0-10V. I have no input sensors connected. How can I program this? Thanks.
Should this be done automatically or manually?
And in which language would you like assistance?
Address 1072 is not valid. For a variable of type word, the highest address you can use is 849.
This looks like some kind of software limitation. However, you can still adjust the analog output value directly via the web interface, and you can select the output from the available range menu.

Hello, The analog output provides only a few milliamps. If your voltage tester has low internal resistance, the measured voltage may drop. Use a multimeter with higher internal resistance for more accurate readings.
It delivers enough current to drive even a panel-mounted 12V LED. I have tested this.
This might help you. Please see the attached possible solution. The analog output requires values between 0 and 1000 for input: 0 units = 0.00 V, 500 units = 5.00 V, 1000 units = 10.00 V.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are exploring how to configure the [company_name] [product_name] analog output to achieve 0-10V without sensors. The discussion highlights programming challenges, memory addressing limitations, software restrictions, how to set output values using the web interface, and issues related to measuring electrical load.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is seeking clear guidance for automatically programming the [product_name] analog output to provide 0-10V. They prefer straightforward methods for setting and monitoring voltage through available software or hardware, and do not want to rely on external sensor inputs.
pain_keywords: incorrect voltage measurement due to test equipment
